questions.q: What is the primary purpose of sub-titling a long piece of writing according to the NCERT textbook?
questions.a: The primary purpose is to convey the main idea or theme of each section so the reader knows at a glance the sub-topics being addressed, and to break the monotony of reading long passages. A wrong answer (e.g., "to make the text look attractive" or "to summarize the whole text in one line") reveals the student confuses sub-titling with formatting or overall summarisation, missing its navigational and structural function.

questions.q: In the article "A new deal for old cities," the author shifts from describing urban decay in India to presenting the Curitiba model. If you were to place a sub-title at the start of the Curitiba paragraph ("The practice in progressive world cities..."), which of these best captures its main idea? (a) Curitiba's Opera House (b) Low-cost urban innovations in Curitiba (c) Bus systems in Brazil (d) Flood management in Mumbai
questions.a: (b) Low-cost urban innovations in Curitiba. This section covers multiple initiatives (car bans, bus system, housing, flood management) unified by the theme of low-cost, innovative planning. Choosing (a) or (c) shows the student latches on to a single detail instead of synthesising the section's central thrust. Choosing (d) indicates confusion between the Indian counter-example and the Curitiba model.

questions.q: Divide the poem "A Photograph" into three sections based on shifts in time perspective and give a sub-title for each section. (Hint: The poem moves from the photograph's past → the mother's past → the poet's present.)
questions.a: Section 1 (Stanza 1): "The Photograph's Frozen Past" — describes the cardboard photo of three girls paddling. Section 2 (Stanza 2): "The Mother's Laughter and Loss" — the mother's later reaction to the photo and her mortality. Section 3 (Stanza 3): "The Poet's Silent Present" — the poet's grief and the silence after the mother's death. A poor answer merges sections or uses vague titles like "Stanza 1," showing inability to detect temporal shifts and thematic focus.

questions.q: Compare the sub-titling needs of a newspaper article (like "A new deal for old cities") and a lyric poem (like "A Photograph"). How does the criterion for dividing sections differ?
questions.a: Newspaper articles are divided by argumentative/logical shifts (problem → example → counter-example → recommendation), so sub-titles track the progression of ideas. A lyric poem is divided by emotional/temporal shifts (past memory → recalled past → present grief), so sub-titles track the movement of consciousness. A student who says "both use paragraphs" misses the genre difference: articles use explicit paragraph breaks; poems use stanzas and tonal turns.

questions.q: Evaluate this set of sub-titles for the article "A new deal for old cities": (1) Urban Decay, (2) Curitiba's Success, (3) Flood Management, (4) Rights-Based Approach. Are they effective? Justify.
questions.a: They are partially effective but flawed. (1) and (4) are strong — noun phrases matching the article's first and last sections. (2) is acceptable but narrow; the Curitiba section covers transport, housing, and floods, not just "success." (3) is a detail, not a section — flood management is one part of the Curitiba section, not a standalone section. The set fails parallelism (mix of broad theme and specific detail) and misrepresents structure by splitting Curitiba's integrated model. A good evaluation notes these structural inaccuracies.

questions.q: Write a 4-section sub-titling plan for a hypothetical article titled "The Vanishing Sparrow: Urban Ecology in Crisis." The article covers: sparrow decline data, causes (architecture, pollution, diet), a success story from a residential colony, and policy recommendations. Ensure parallel structure.
questions.a: (1) Documenting the Sparrow Decline (2) Analysing the Causes of Disappearance (3) Showcasing a Community-Led Revival (4) Recommending Policy Interventions. All use gerund phrases, parallel and comprehensive. A poor answer uses mismatched forms ("Sparrow Numbers," "Why They Die," "A Happy Story," "What Government Should Do") revealing weak grasp of parallelism and inability to generalise from specific content.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Sub-titling is the skill of dividing a text into logical sections and assigning each a concise, ______ heading that captures its central idea, enabling readers to navigate the text efficiently and grasp its structural progression at a glance.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you open a 10-page history chapter the night before an exam and feel overwhelmed by the dense ______.
What is Sub-titling? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Sub-titling is the skill of dividing a text into logical sections and assigning each a concise, descriptive heading that captures its central idea, enabling readers to navigate the text efficiently and grasp its structural progression at a glance.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine you open a ______-page history chapter the night before an exam and feel overwhelmed by the dense paragraphs.
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Sub-titling?
questions.a: Students believe sub-titling is simply labelling paragraphs with the first noun phrase they spot (e.g., "Curitiba" or "Floods").

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can independently segment any unfamiliar prose text (article, essay, report) into 3-5 coherent sections based on shifts in sub-topic, argument, or perspective, and compose a sub-title for each section that is accurate, parallel in structure, and limited to 4-6 words.
